text:
maria: Heads up — mkdocs build failing on prod docs site after moving the ops guide into a symlinked package. CI shows duplicate fragment IDs.

docs-bot: build failed: Duplicate ID found: 'getting-started' in 'site/guides/ops/setup.html' and 'site/guides/setup.html'

alex: I ran into this before. Symlinked files end up rendered twice (two source paths), slugify produces same heading IDs.

ryan: Can you paste the exact mkdocs output and the file paths? Might be a slugify/plugin config issue.

maria: Error snippet:
```
ERROR    -  Duplicate ID found: 'getting-started' in 'site/guides/ops/setup.html'
ERROR    -  Duplicate ID found: 'getting-started' in 'site/guides/setup.html'
```

susan: Quick options: 1) change URLs (use_directory_urls: false) 2) add a frontmatter slug/permalink to the duplicated file 3) remove the symlink and copy the file.

alex: We should avoid url changes. I prefer adding frontmatter only for the symlinked copy: `slug: ops-setup` or `permalink: /guides/ops/setup/`. Small and reversible.

maria: I don't love modifying user-facing permalinks either, but this is narrow. I opened PR #3321 with a `slug: ops-setup` frontmatter on the ops copy and fixed a broken code fence at the same time. Local mkdocs build passes. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3321

docs-bot: preview build available: https://deploy.preview/4765432199-3321 — anchors now unique, no duplicate-id warnings.

ryan: Can we also add a CI check to catch duplicate anchors early? A lightweight script that runs `mkdocs build` and greps for "Duplicate ID" would do.

susan: Yes please. Add it to the docs workflow as a separate step so it fails fast. Also log full paths to help triage.

alex: I'll add `tools/docs/validate_anchors.py` that parses the mkdocs stdout and exits non-zero on duplicates, then wire it into .github/workflows/docs.yml. I'll try to keep it <50 lines.

maria: Another related issue: during the migration one of the fenced bash blocks lost its leading spaces and rendered inline. I fixed that in the PR by using explicit triple backticks with `bash`.

ryan: Nice. After you add the CI guard I'll run a couple of other symlink permutations locally. If green, we can merge.

alex: Pushed the validate_anchors script and workflow tweak in a followup commit. PR updated.

maria: Thanks — leaving a note in the migration guide about symlink caveats and anchor collisions so future moves check for this.

alex: Merging now :shipit:

docs-bot: pull request merged by alex — commit abc123def (4765432215)

maria: great, closing the loop. I'll monitor the scheduled site build tomorrow for any regressions. :+1:
